scenes.title: The World Around Us
narration: Have you ever wondered what makes up your skin, a tree, or a tasty mango?
Everything alive is made of teeny-tiny parts called cells.
They are so small that you need a special microscope to see them clearly.

scenes.title: What Is A Cell?
narration: Think of a cell like a single brick in a giant school building.
Each cell has a special job to keep the whole body working.
Some cells help you move, while others help you digest your breakfast.

scenes.title: Cells At Work
narration: Let us look at your own skin cells protecting you like a suit of armor.
Inside, your red blood cells carry oxygen to your toes and fingers.
They travel through tiny tubes to make sure your body stays strong.

scenes.title: Recap And Explore
narration: Cells are the smallest building blocks of all living things.
Groups of cells work together to form your body parts.
Think about it: If your body is made of billions of cells, how do they all know what to do?

scenes.title: The Tiny Building Blocks
narration: Have you ever looked at a tiny leaf or a mango seed?
Everything alive is made of tiny, invisible building blocks called cells.
Think of them like little rooms that make up all living creatures.

scenes.title: Parts of the Cell
narration: Every cell has a control center called the nucleus that tells it what to do.
The jelly-like cytoplasm fills the space and keeps everything safe inside.
A thin cell membrane acts like a gatekeeper, letting good stuff in and out.

scenes.title: Plants vs Animals
narration: A plant cell has a stiff cell wall to help it stand tall.
Plant cells also have green chloroplasts to turn sunlight into delicious food.
Animal cells do not have walls, which is why we are soft and wiggly.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Remember, all living things are made of cells that work together.
Plants have walls and chloroplasts, while animal cells do not.
Think about it: if you were a plant, where would you get your energy from?

scenes.title: The Meadow Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered why grass grows and what keeps animals full?
In a sunny park in Delhi, everything is connected by what they eat.
Let us explore how energy moves from the sun to your dinner plate.

scenes.title: Building a Food Chain
narration: It all starts with plants, which are producers that make their own food.
A hungry grasshopper eats the green grass to get its energy.
Then, a fast frog catches the grasshopper for a tasty snack.
Finally, a snake slides in to eat the frog, completing the chain.

scenes.title: The Tangled Food Web
narration: But wait, nature is not just one straight line of eating.
Many animals eat different things, forming a messy, wonderful food web.
If one piece disappears, like if the grass dies, the whole web shakes.

scenes.title: Nature's Amazing Circle
narration: Producers make energy, and consumers pass it along the food chain.
Everything in our ecosystem plays a special role to stay healthy.
Think about it: what would happen to the web if we lost all the snakes?

scenes.title: Where do babies come from?
narration: Have you ever wondered how a tiny seed grows into a big mango tree?
Or why your puppy looks just like its mother?
This amazing process is called reproduction.

scenes.title: How life creates life
narration: Reproduction is how living things make new versions of themselves.
Some animals like birds lay eggs that hatch into chicks.
Others, like humans or cows, give birth to live young ones.
Plants use seeds or cuttings to start their new lives.

scenes.title: The mango tree example
narration: Let us look at a juicy mango tree in a village garden.
The flowers on the tree get pollinated by buzzy bees.
The flower turns into a fruit containing a hard seed inside.
When that seed falls into the soil, it sprouts into a tiny plant.

scenes.title: Wrapping it all up
narration: Every living thing follows a cycle to make sure life continues.
Whether through eggs, seeds, or birth, reproduction keeps nature moving.
Think about it: what would happen to our world if nothing could reproduce?

scenes.title: The Web of Life
narration: Look at the busy park near your home in Delhi.
Did you know that all these living things are connected?
How does a tiny squirrel depend on the big banyan tree?

scenes.title: What is an Ecosystem
narration: An ecosystem is a community of living things working together.
Living things are called biotic factors, like plants and animals.
Non-living things like sunlight and water are abiotic factors.
They all rely on each other to stay healthy and strong.

scenes.title: A Pond Example
narration: Let us look at a pond in a quiet village.
The sun helps the pond weeds grow, which feed the fish.
Tiny insects eat the weeds, and a frog eats the insects.
Even the mud at the bottom helps clean the water.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Every ecosystem needs biotic and abiotic parts to survive.
When one part changes, the whole system feels it.
Think about it: what would happen to the pond if the sun stopped shining?

scenes.title: A Tiny Mystery
narration: Have you ever seen a tiny egg on a leaf in your garden, Rohan?
That small egg is the start of an incredible journey for a butterfly.
How does a crawling creature turn into something that can fly?

scenes.title: Four Magical Stages
narration: First, the tiny egg hatches into a hungry caterpillar.
The caterpillar eats leaves and grows bigger every single day.
Then, it builds a hard shell called a chrysalis around itself.
Inside the chrysalis, its body changes completely in a process called metamorphosis.

scenes.title: The Beautiful Transformation
narration: Finally, the shell breaks open to reveal a colorful butterfly.
Priya sees it drying its wings in the warm Indian sun.
It flies away to find nectar and lay eggs to start again.

scenes.title: Remembering the Cycle
narration: So, the stages are egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, and adult butterfly.
Every butterfly follows this exact same path to grow up.
Think about it: which stage do you think is the hardest work for the butterfly?

scenes.title: Why Animals Look Different
narration: Have you ever wondered why a camel has a humpy back while a fish has fins?
Animals have special features called adaptations that help them live in their homes.
Without these traits, they would find it very hard to survive in the wild.

scenes.title: Understanding Animal Adaptations
narration: Adaptations can be body parts, like sharp claws for catching food.
They can also be clever behaviors, like birds flying south for warmer weather.
These changes happen over a very long time to help animals thrive.

scenes.title: Example: The Desert Camel
narration: Take the camel in the Thar desert; it has wide feet to walk on sand.
Its long eyelashes keep out the blowing sand when the wind picks up.
It even stores fat in its hump to use as energy when food is scarce.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Adaptations are body parts or behaviors that help animals survive in their environment.
Whether in the desert or the deep ocean, nature gives every creature a superpower.
Think about it: what adaptation do you think helps a polar bear stay warm?

scenes.title: Why So Many Creatures?
narration: Look at Arjun's garden, it has ladybugs, birds, and sunflowers.
Why do we need so many different living things together?
This variety of life is called biodiversity.

scenes.title: Nature is a Team
narration: Think of nature like a big, complex spider web.
Every plant and animal has a special job to do.
Bees pollinate flowers to help our fruits grow.
Fungi break down dead leaves into healthy soil.

scenes.title: A Healthy Forest Example
narration: In a forest, trees provide homes for monkeys and birds.
If a sickness hurts the trees, the birds lose their home.
But if many types of trees exist, the birds stay safe.
Biodiversity keeps the forest strong and healthy.

scenes.title: Protecting Our Planet
narration: Biodiversity means every creature helps the whole world work.
We must protect habitats so every species can survive.
Can you spot three different insects in your park today?

scenes.title: The Big Question
narration: Have you ever wondered where your tasty samosa goes after you eat it?
It travels through a long, winding tube inside your body to give you energy.
This process is called digestion, and it is like a magical recycling factory.

scenes.title: How Digestion Works
narration: First, your teeth chew the food into small, soft pieces.
Then, spit mixes with the food to make it easy to swallow.
The food slides down your throat into your stretchy stomach.
In the stomach, juices break the food down into a thick soup.

scenes.title: From Soup to Energy
narration: Next, the soup moves into the long, curly small intestine.
Here, your body pulls out all the good nutrients like vitamins.
These nutrients enter your blood to help you run and play.
Finally, the leftover bits leave your body as waste.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Digestion turns your lunch into the energy you need every single day.
Remember, teeth, stomach, and intestines all work together as a team.
Think about it: Why do you think it is important to chew your food slowly?

scenes.title: The Big Breath In
narration: Have you ever wondered why you need to breathe every single second?
Even when you are playing cricket in the park, your body needs air.
Let us look at how oxygen enters your body to help you move.

scenes.title: The Journey Inside
narration: The air travels down your throat into two spongy bags called lungs.
Inside the lungs, tiny tubes branch out like the roots of a tree.
At the very end, oxygen passes into your blood to travel everywhere.
Your blood carries this oxygen to give your muscles energy to run.

scenes.title: The Exchange Process
narration: Imagine you have five rupees to trade for a tasty mango.
Your blood trades carbon dioxide for fresh oxygen in the lungs.
The carbon dioxide is waste that your body wants to get rid of.
You breathe out to push that waste air back into the world.

scenes.title: Staying Healthy Always
narration: Your lungs work hard all day and night without stopping.
Eating healthy food and running helps keep your lungs super strong.
Think about it: how do you feel after running a fast race?

Nervous System.title: Your Body's Super Fast Message System

scenes.title: The Instant Reaction Hook
narration: Have you ever pulled your hand away quickly after touching a hot tea cup?
That happens in a blink of an eye without you even thinking about it.
How does your body know to move so fast?

scenes.title: Meet the Command Center
narration: Your brain acts like a powerful computer that controls everything you do.
Nerves are like tiny wires that carry messages all through your body.
The spinal cord is the main highway that connects the brain to the nerves.
Together, they form your amazing nervous system.

scenes.title: How a Message Travels
narration: First, your finger feels the heat from the hot cup.
A message zooms along your nerves to your spinal cord.
The brain says danger, so it sends a command back instantly.
Your muscles pull your hand away to keep you safe.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up
narration: Your brain, spinal cord, and nerves work together to keep you safe.
They help you sense the world, move, and even think about your favorite food.
Think about it: what other things does your nervous system help you do today?

scenes.title: The Body's Busy Highway
narration: Have you ever wondered how energy from your breakfast reaches your toes so quickly?
It happens because of your amazing circulatory system, a network of hidden tubes inside you.
Your heart acts like a powerful pump to push blood through your whole body.

scenes.title: How Blood Moves Around
narration: Blood travels through tubes called arteries, which carry fresh oxygen to your muscles.
After dropping off oxygen, blood returns to the heart through tubes called veins.
The heart keeps the blood moving in a big, endless loop day and night.

scenes.title: An Example of Flow
narration: Imagine Rohan running a race at his school in Delhi.
His heart beats faster to send more oxygen-rich blood to his tired legs.
His blood picks up waste like carbon dioxide to bring back to the lungs.
Once he breathes out, his blood is ready to start its journey again.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up Our Journey
narration: The circulatory system uses the heart, arteries, and veins to keep you moving.
It delivers important food and oxygen while cleaning out the waste from your body.
Think about it: how many times do you think your heart beats in just one minute?

scenes.title: The Body's Hidden Framework
narration: Have you ever wondered how Rohan stands tall without folding like a piece of paper?
Under your skin, there is a strong frame called the skeleton.
It is made of two hundred and six hard bones that protect your organs.

scenes.title: How Muscles Help Us Move
narration: But bones cannot move alone, they need help from your muscles.
Muscles are like stretchy rubber bands attached to your bones.
When a muscle pulls on a bone, your arm or leg moves.
This constant pulling and pushing is how you run and play cricket.

scenes.title: Bending Your Arm
narration: Let us look at your bicep muscle when you lift a heavy school bag.
As you lift, the bicep muscle gets shorter and thicker.
This pulls your forearm bone upward toward your shoulder.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Your skeleton provides the shape, while muscles provide the movement.
Together, they make you a strong, moving machine.
Think about it, what would happen if your bones were soft like jelly?

scenes.title: The Curious Apple
narration: Have you ever dropped a juicy mango from your hand while eating lunch?
It does not float away, but falls straight down to the floor.
Have you ever wondered what invisible force is pulling it down?

scenes.title: Understanding the Invisible Force
narration: That invisible pull is called gravity, a force that attracts objects together.
Everything with mass has gravity, but big things like Earth pull much harder.
Because Earth is huge, it acts like a giant magnet for everything nearby.

scenes.title: Gravity in Action
narration: Let us imagine Rohan kicks a football high into the sky.
As the ball climbs, gravity works to slow its speed down.
Once it stops rising, gravity pulls it back down to the grass.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up
narration: So, gravity keeps our feet on the ground and brings falling things home.
Without this constant tug, we would all be floating in space!
Think about it: how would playing cricket be different if Earth had no gravity?

scenes.title: The Energy Mystery
narration: Aarav feels tired during cricket practice despite eating breakfast.
Why does our body need specific fuel to keep playing?
Let us discover how to keep your energy levels high.

scenes.title: The Healthy Plate Rules
narration: Carbohydrates like roti give you quick energy for running.
Proteins like dal help your muscles grow big and strong.
Vegetables provide vitamins to keep you from getting sick.
Water is the magic liquid that keeps everything flowing smoothly.

scenes.title: Building Aarav's Lunch
narration: First, add a warm roti for carbohydrates.
Next, add a big bowl of healthy dal for protein.
Finally, add crisp cucumber salad for vitamins.
Now Aarav has the perfect meal to win his match.

scenes.title: Stay Strong Daily
narration: Eat a colorful plate to get all your nutrients.
Drink plenty of water and stay active every single day.
Think about it, what healthy snack will you choose today?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Stopping
narration: Have you ever wondered why your bicycle stops when you stop pedaling?
Imagine Rohan sliding a carrom striker across a smooth board.
It slides fast, but eventually, it always comes to a stop.

scenes.title: Understanding Friction
narration: This invisible force that stops moving objects is called friction.
It happens when two surfaces rub against each other.
Even surfaces that look smooth have tiny bumps and ridges.
These bumps catch on each other, acting like tiny brakes.

scenes.title: Real World Friction
narration: Think of wearing sneakers with patterns on the rubber soles.
Those patterns create more friction so you do not slip.
If you walked on a wet floor, there is less friction.
That is why you might slide and fall down!

scenes.title: Friction Recap
narration: Friction is a force that opposes motion between surfaces.
Rougher surfaces create more friction than smooth ones.
Without it, we could not walk or stop our cars.
Think about it: could you play a game of cricket without friction?

scenes.title: Where does light come from?
narration: Have you ever wondered how you see your cricket bat in the dark?
Light travels in a straight line from a source, like the sun.
Objects like a glowing bulb or a candle are light sources.

scenes.title: How we see things
narration: Light hits an object and bounces off it into our eyes.
This bouncing back is what scientists call reflection.
Without this bounce, everything would look completely invisible to us.

scenes.title: A Mirror Experiment
narration: Let us try this with a mirror and a flashlight.
Aim your light at the mirror and watch it hit the wall.
The angle it hits is the same angle it bounces off.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Light travels straight and bounces off objects so we can see.
Mirrors are great at reflecting light because they are very smooth.
Think about it: why do you see your face in a mirror but not on a wall?

scenes.title: The Energy All Around Us
narration: Have you ever wondered how your bicycle moves or why a lamp lights up?
Everything we do needs energy to make it happen.
Energy is simply the ability to do work or cause change.

scenes.title: Different Types of Energy
narration: Energy comes in many forms, like the heat from your morning chai.
When you run in the park, you use stored energy from your food.
Objects in motion, like a rolling ball, have kinetic energy.
And light energy helps us see everything around us.

scenes.title: Energy In Action
narration: Let us look at a mixer grinder in the kitchen.
First, electrical energy travels through the wire into the machine.
Then, it changes into mechanical energy to spin the blades.
Finally, the machine makes a sound, showing energy can change forms.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up Energy
narration: Energy is everywhere and it helps us move, grow, and see.
Remember, energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed.
Think about it, what forms of energy do you see in your house today?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Sound
narration: Have you ever wondered how your friend's voice reaches your ears from across the playground?
When Rohan claps his hands, he creates a special kind of movement called a vibration.
These vibrations travel through the air like invisible ripples in a pond.

scenes.title: How Sound Waves Move
narration: Sound waves push the air particles forward in a chain reaction.
The particles bump into each other, passing the energy along until it hits your ear.
Sound needs a medium like air, water, or even solid wood to travel.
In outer space where there is no air, sound cannot travel at all.

scenes.title: Testing at Home
narration: Let us test this with a metal spoon and a string tied to a table.
When you strike the spoon against the table, sound travels through the string.
Hold the string to your ear and you will hear a loud, clear ringing sound.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: Sound is just vibration energy traveling as waves through a medium.
Remember, without air or another solid object, sound cannot move to your ears.
Think about it: Why do you think a whale's sound travels so far underwater?

scenes.title: The Magic Switch
narration: Have you ever wondered how flicking a switch turns on the fan in your room?
It happens because electricity travels through wires hidden inside your walls.
Today, let's explore how this invisible energy gets to your home.

scenes.title: The Path of Electrons
narration: Electricity is actually a flow of tiny particles called electrons moving through a material.
These electrons need a complete path to travel on, which we call a circuit.
If the path is broken, the electricity stops moving and your light goes out.

scenes.title: From Power Station to Bulb
narration: Imagine electricity starting at a big power plant, maybe using coal or sunlight.
It travels across tall metal towers to reach your neighborhood transformer.
Finally, it enters your house wires and powers your study lamp in an instant.

scenes.title: Summary and Think
narration: Electricity needs a complete circuit path to flow and power our devices.
Always remember that electricity is powerful and can be dangerous if touched directly.
Think about it: What would your day look like if the electricity went out right now?

scenes.title: The Magic Flashlight Switch
narration: Have you ever wondered how your flashlight turns on with just a click?
It all happens because of something called an electric circuit.
Let us see how electricity travels to make the bulb glow.

scenes.title: Parts Of A Circuit
narration: First, we need a power source like a battery to push energy.
Next, we need wires to act as a path for electricity.
Finally, the bulb turns energy into light for us to see.
If the path is broken, the electricity stops moving completely.

scenes.title: Building A Simple Circuit
narration: Imagine connecting a small 9-volt battery to a tiny LED light.
When you touch the wire to both sides of the battery, the path closes.
The electricity flows, and your light shines bright in the room.
Remove one wire, and the light goes out instantly.

scenes.title: Recap And Explore
narration: A circuit needs a battery, wires, and a bulb to work.
Electricity only travels when the path is a complete loop.
Think about it: why do you think we use plastic to cover our electric wires?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Movement
narration: Have you ever wondered why your cricket ball stops rolling on the grass?
Or why your bicycle moves faster when you pedal harder?
Everything moving around us is controlled by invisible actions called forces.

scenes.title: Push and Pull
narration: A force is simply a push or a pull on an object.
When you push a shopping trolley at the market, you make it move away.
When you pull a drawer open to get your socks, you make it come toward you.
Forces can change the speed, direction, or shape of an object.

scenes.title: Stopping the Ball
narration: Let us look at Rohan kicking a football across the field.
His foot gives the ball a push force to start its motion.
As it rolls, friction from the grass acts as a force pulling against it.
Because friction resists motion, the ball eventually slows down and stops.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up
narration: Remember, a push or pull is a force that changes how things move.
Friction is a special force that slows objects down when they rub together.
Think about it: if there were no friction, would you ever be able to stop running?

scenes.title: The Fridge Door Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered why your drawing stays stuck to the fridge door?
A hidden force keeps the paper in place without any glue or tape.
This invisible power is called magnetism, and it is everywhere around us.

scenes.title: How Magnets Work
narration: Every magnet has two ends called the North pole and the South pole.
When you bring two magnets together, opposite poles pull toward each other.
But if you try to join matching poles, they push each other away.

scenes.title: Testing Your Toys
narration: Let us test a steel spoon, a plastic toy, and an iron coin.
The magnet pulls the iron coin and the steel spoon strongly.
The plastic toy stays still because magnets only attract certain metals.

scenes.title: Magnets Recap
narration: Magnets have two poles and use invisible forces to push or pull metals.
They only stick to objects made of materials like iron or steel.
Think about it: can you find three things in your kitchen that magnets stick to?

scenes.title: What is everything made of?
narration: Have you ever wondered why your steel lunchbox is hard but your water is splashy?
Everything around us, from the trees to your toys, is called matter.
Matter is made of tiny, tiny pieces that are always moving.

scenes.title: Solids, Liquids, and Gases
narration: In a solid, particles are packed tight and barely move at all.
In a liquid, particles slide past each other easily so it can flow.
In a gas, particles zoom around everywhere with lots of space between them.

scenes.title: The Ice Cube Story
narration: Watch a frozen ice cube from your freezer sitting on a warm plate.
Heat makes the solid particles wiggle faster until they turn into liquid water.
If you boil that water, it turns into steam, which is a gas.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up
narration: Solids keep their shape, liquids take the shape of their container, and gases fill everything.
Everything you touch is either a solid, a liquid, or a gas.
Think about it: can you find something in your room that is a gas?

scenes.title: The Ice Cube Mystery
narration: Have you ever watched an ice cube melt in your juice on a hot afternoon?
Does the water taste different, or is it still just water?
Let us discover why some things change shape but stay the same inside.

scenes.title: What is a Physical Change?
narration: A physical change happens when matter changes its look, but not its identity.
You can rip a piece of paper, but it is still paper.
Crushing a soda can changes its shape, but it is still metal.
These changes are often easy to reverse, like freezing water back into ice.

scenes.title: Making Lemonade at Home
narration: Imagine you have a glass of water and add a spoonful of sugar.
Stir it well until the sugar dissolves into the water.
The sugar is still there, just hidden in the water.
Because no new substance was created, this is a physical change.

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: Physical changes alter appearance but do not create new materials.
Remember, melting, freezing, and dissolving are all common physical changes.
Think about it: is chopping vegetables for dinner a physical change?

scenes.title: The Kitchen Mystery
narration: Have you ever seen your mother toast a slice of bread for breakfast?
It starts soft and white, but ends up brown, crunchy, and smelling delicious.
Can we turn that brown toast back into soft white bread? No way!

scenes.title: What is a Chemical Change?
narration: A chemical change happens when substances combine to create something brand new.
The new material has different properties than the things we started with.
Unlike ripping paper, these changes are usually permanent and cannot be undone.
We see signs like bubbles, color changes, or heat being released.

scenes.title: Squeezing Lemon Juice
narration: Imagine mixing lemon juice with baking soda in a small bowl.
Suddenly, you see fizzy bubbles forming right before your very eyes.
The bubbles are a new gas being created by the chemical reaction.
Since we cannot turn the bubbles back into soda and juice, it is chemical.

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: Chemical changes make new substances that are impossible to turn back.
Look for bubbles, heat, or color changes to spot them happening.
Think about it: Is rusting iron left out in the rain a chemical change?

scenes.title: The Kitchen Mystery
narration: Have you ever made a glass of nimbu pani for a hot afternoon?
You mix sugar and lemon into water, but where does the sugar go?
Today we will discover how mixing things creates mixtures and solutions.

scenes.title: What Are Mixtures?
narration: A mixture is when two or more things are combined together.
In a bowl of bhel puri, you can still see the puffed rice and sev.
These parts do not change their identity, even when they are mixed.

scenes.title: Making A Solution
narration: A solution is special because one part dissolves into the other.
The substance that dissolves is called the solute, like salt.
The water is the solvent that lets the salt disappear inside it.
Now the salt is spread evenly throughout the water.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Remember, mixtures keep parts separate, but solutions blend them perfectly.
Science is all around us in the kitchen and the lab.
Think about it, can you separate a solution like salty water back into salt?

scenes.title: The Daily Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered why your lunchbox is plastic but your spoon is metal?
Why does a raincoat keep you dry while your cotton shirt gets soaked?
Everything we use has special properties that make it perfect for the job.

scenes.title: What Makes A Material?
narration: Hardness is how tough a material is against scratches.
Transparency lets light pass through, like glass in a window.
Flexibility means it can bend without snapping into pieces.
And some materials, like copper wires, let electricity flow right through them.

scenes.title: Testing A Raincoat
narration: Let us test if a raincoat is waterproof for a rainy day in Mumbai.
We pour a glass of water onto the surface of the coat.
The water beads up and rolls off because plastic is non-porous.
If we used paper, it would soak up the water and tear.

scenes.title: Summary And Challenge
narration: Materials have different properties like hardness, flexibility, and transparency.
Choosing the right material keeps us safe and makes life easier.
Think about it: why are cooking pans made of metal but their handles made of plastic?

scenes.title: Looking Up at the Sky
narration: Have you ever looked at the night sky and wondered what else is out there?
Our sun is actually a giant star at the center of our neighborhood.
Eight planets and many smaller objects travel around it in a big cosmic dance.

scenes.title: The Planets in Order
narration: Mercury is closest, followed by Venus and our home, Earth.
Next is Mars, known as the red planet, and giant Jupiter.
Then Saturn with its rings, followed by icy Uranus and Neptune.
Gravity is the invisible force that keeps them all in their paths.

scenes.title: A Trip to Mars
narration: Imagine we are traveling from Earth to visit Mars for a research mission.
It takes many months to fly across the dark, silent space between them.
When we arrive, we see red dust, giant volcanoes, and frozen polar ice caps.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: We have one star and eight unique planets held together by gravity.
Everything moves in a perfect, repeating cycle around the Sun.
If you could visit any planet, which one would you choose and why?

scenes.title: The Mystery Under Our Feet
narration: Have you ever picked up a cool stone while playing at the park?
Did you know those rocks are actually super old puzzles?
Let us discover how they are made and what is inside them.

scenes.title: The Three Main Types
narration: First, igneous rocks form when hot lava from a volcano cools down.
Second, sedimentary rocks form as layers of sand press together over time.
Third, metamorphic rocks change shape because of intense heat and pressure.

scenes.title: Spotting Minerals in Nature
narration: Look at this piece of granite from a kitchen counter in Mumbai.
It is made of different minerals like quartz, feldspar, and mica.
Minerals are the solid building blocks that give rocks their colors.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Rocks come from heat, layers, or pressure, and minerals are their ingredients.
Next time you find a pebble, look closely for shiny mineral spots.
Can you guess why some rocks are smooth and others are rough?

scenes.title: Where does rain go?
narration: Have you ever wondered why puddles disappear after a sunny day in your school playground?
Does the water just vanish into thin air, or does it go on a secret journey?
Let us follow a drop of water through the cycle that keeps our Earth hydrated.

scenes.title: How water rises up
narration: When the sun warms up the river near your house, water turns into invisible gas called vapor.
This process is called evaporation, as the water rises high into the blue sky.
As it gets higher, the air becomes cooler and the vapor turns back into tiny liquid drops.
These millions of tiny drops bunch together to form the fluffy white clouds we see.

scenes.title: Rain in Mumbai
narration: Think of a rainy day in Mumbai when the heavy clouds get too full and dark.
Gravity pulls the water down as rain, or sometimes even as cold hail, toward the ground.
This water flows into streams, rivers, and eventually fills up our big lakes again.

scenes.title: Nature's endless loop
narration: The water cycle is a never-ending loop of evaporation, condensation, and rain that refreshes our planet.
Without this cycle, our crops would not grow and we would not have clean water to drink.
Think about it: if you drank a glass of water today, could it be the same water a dinosaur drank?

scenes.title: The World Around Us
narration: Look around your kitchen, Rohan; where do your water, food, and electricity actually come from?
These things are called natural resources, and they are gifts from our amazing planet Earth.
Have you ever wondered if these gifts will last forever if we use them every single day?

scenes.title: Renewable Versus Non-renewable
narration: Some resources like sunlight and wind are renewable, meaning they never run out.
Others like coal used in power plants take millions of years to form underground.
Because they take so long, we call them non-renewable; once they are gone, they are gone.

scenes.title: Saving Our Precious Water
narration: Take water, for example, which we need to drink, wash clothes, and grow our rice crops.
If we leave the tap running while brushing our teeth, we waste this precious resource.
By turning the tap off, we save liters of water for others in our community.

scenes.title: Be a Resource Hero
narration: Remember, natural resources are either renewable or non-renewable, so we must use them carefully.
Reduce what you use, reuse your old notebooks, and recycle paper to help our Earth stay healthy.
Think about it: what is one thing you can stop wasting at school today?

Climate and Environment.title: Why Does The Earth Get Warm?

scenes.title: A Hotter Afternoon
narration: Have you noticed how hot the afternoons in Delhi feel lately?
The sun is strong, but why does the air feel like a warm blanket?
Let us find out why our planet is getting a little bit feverish.

scenes.title: The Greenhouse Effect
narration: The Earth is wrapped in a layer of invisible gases called the atmosphere.
These gases act like the glass walls of a greenhouse for plants.
They trap heat from the sun to keep us nice and cozy.

scenes.title: Too Much Of A Good Thing
narration: When we burn coal or petrol for cars, we release more gases.
Imagine wearing a thick wool sweater on a hot summer day.
That is exactly what we are doing to our poor Earth.

scenes.title: Helping Our Home
narration: To help, we can plant more trees and save electricity at home.
Small steps like these keep our air clean and our planet cool.
Think about it: how can you save energy in your room today?

scenes.title: The Night Sky Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered why the moon looks different every night from your balcony in Delhi?
Sometimes it is a bright circle, and other times it is just a tiny glowing sliver.
Let us discover how the moon travels around our home planet, Earth.

scenes.title: Orbiting Our Planet
narration: The moon is Earth's only natural satellite, which means it travels in a circle around us.
It takes about twenty-seven days for the moon to complete one full trip around Earth.
While it travels, the sun lights up different parts of the moon's surface.

scenes.title: Seeing the Phases
narration: When the moon is between Earth and the sun, the side facing us is dark.
As it moves, we see more of the sunlit side, eventually becoming a full, round moon.
Think of it like a flashlight shining on a ball from different angles.

scenes.title: Summary and Wonder
narration: The moon orbits Earth, and its changing shape depends on where it is in that path.
It is Earth's best friend in space, keeping us company every single night.
If the moon disappeared tomorrow, what do you think would happen to our nights?

scenes.title: The Changing Weather
narration: Have you noticed how hot summers are and how chilly winters feel in Delhi?
Why does the weather change so much throughout the year?
Let us explore why the Earth dances through different seasons.

scenes.title: The Tilted Earth
narration: Our Earth is not straight up and down; it is tilted on an axis.
As Earth travels around the Sun, different parts get more direct sunlight.
When your part of Earth tilts toward the Sun, it is summer time.
When it tilts away, we experience the cooler winter months.

scenes.title: A Year of Changes
narration: Imagine Earth is at one side, tilted toward the Sun's warm rays.
The days get longer and we get heat for our summer holidays.
Six months later, Earth has moved to the opposite side of its orbit.
Now our part is tilted away, making the days short and chilly.

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: Seasons happen because Earth is tilted while it orbits the Sun.
Tilt decides how much heat each part of the world receives.
Think about it: what season would it be if Earth had no tilt at all?

scenes.title: A Day at the Park
narration: Have you noticed how the sun plays hide and seek in the park every evening?
Arjun wonders, does the sun actually move, or is it something else?
Let us discover how our Earth keeps spinning to change the time.

scenes.title: The Earth is Spinning
narration: Our Earth is a giant ball that is always spinning like a spinning top.
This spinning motion is called rotation, and it takes twenty-four hours to complete.
Because it is a sphere, the sun can only light up one side at once.
The side facing the sun enjoys bright, sunny daytime.

scenes.title: Night in Mumbai
narration: Imagine it is noon in Mumbai and the sun is high above.
As the Earth spins, Mumbai slowly moves away from the sun's direct light.
Now, the city is in its own shadow, which we call night.
We see the stars clearly because the sun is shining on the other side.

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: The sun stays still while the Earth rotates on its axis.
Day happens when we face the sun, and night happens when we turn away.
Think about it, if Earth stopped spinning, what would happen to our days?
